key_observations: STABILITY GATE FAILED — fell_over_rate = 1.60 in the final window (iters ~616–769), well past the Rule 2 threshold of iter 750. The slope is -0.0016/iter (slowly declining) but the run only reached 769 of 3000 planned iterations, so this never had a chance to recover. This is a genuine stability failure, not early-training noise.

HYPOTHESIS REFUTED — The hypothesis attributed run 1's instability entirely to angular_momentum_reward_weight = -0.05. This run reverted that term to -0.01 but still failed stability at the same severity. The destabilising force is gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight = -2.5, not angular momentum. A rigid rhythm penalty prevents the robot from taking corrective recovery steps when off-balance.

gait_contact_cv_mean WORSENED, not improved — it trended upward from 0.334 (start) to 0.567 (end), with a positive slope (+1.93e-5/iter). This is the same poor value as the original baseline. The stronger regularity penalty failed its primary intended effect and is actively fighting the policy's ability to manage stance timing.
gait_air_cv_mean was flat (0.247 → 0.260) — no improvement on the swing CV metric either. Both CV targets missed.

Locomotion speed = 0.085 m/s is extremely low. The policy is barely moving. Rule 5 applies: the curriculum is likely still at a low command velocity stage, so tracking reward values (1.16) are not a reliable signal of real capability. The robot is surviving very short bouts rather than walking.

Entropy health is acceptable — final entropy is 19.94 vs starting 28.29 (70.5% of starting value), above the ~30% collapse threshold. mean_action_std = 0.664, far from the over-deterministic floor of 0.1. Exploration is not the problem.
landing_force_mean = 40.9 N is healthy (Rule 8 range: 30–90 N). No reason to touch soft_landing weight.

Rule 6 side-effect check: gait_phase_regularity reward achieved -1.51 against weight -2.5, implying the policy is pushing hard against the regularity term but still failing to produce regular timing — while simultaneously losing balance. The weight is consuming learning capacity without delivering the CV reduction it was supposed to produce.
next_suggestion: Back off gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight from -2.5 to -1.0 (a moderate step up from baseline, not a 5× jump). Keep pose_std_walking_shoulder_pitch = 0.35 (arm freedom is harmless and should stay). Keep angular_momentum_reward_weight = -0.01 (confirmed not the culprit). This isolates whether a gentler regularity nudge can improve CV without overriding stabilising reflexes. Expected side-effect to verify per Rule 6: track_linear_velocity should dip slightly vs. baseline if the regularity weight is doing real work — if it doesn't move at all, the weight is still too weak to have effect. Stability gate (fell_over < 0.5 past iter 750) is the primary pass criterion; only evaluate CV improvement if that gate passes.
